Writing a sheet

A sheet is a list of statements, one per line or separated by semicolons. Dome solves the sheet as a system: the order of the lines does not matter, and an unknown may sit on either side of an equation. This page follows the first example, Help › Examples › First sheet: equations and units.

Equations and units

p   = 2 [bar]
V_1 = 40 [L]
T_1 = 27 [C]
W   = 6 [kJ]
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)
T_2 / T_1 = V_2 / V_1
  • Equations. a = b in any arrangement. Dome matches equations to unknowns, evaluates the explicit ones directly and solves the rest by iteration. Equations that repeat each other, contradict each other or leave a variable undetermined are reported on their line.
  • Units. A unit follows a number in square brackets. Everything after a slash is in the denominator, so [kJ/kg·K] is kJ/(kg·K); *, ^ and parentheses also work. Values are converted to SI on entry, so bar, kPa, L and kJ can be mixed. A number without a unit where one is needed is an error, except 0, which is zero in any unit: a balance can be written as the book writes it, 0 = Q - W + mdot*(h_1 - h_2), and W takes the unit of the other terms. A 0 set equal to a temperature still needs a unit, since 0 °C and 0 K differ. A number without a unit where nothing requires one is a plain number: with W_net = 100 and W_net = mdot*(h_1 - h_2), mdot comes out in s^2/m^2. A result in a unit that no usual quantity has is warned on when a number written without a unit explains it, through a root too (V in V = sqrt(2*KE/m) with KE = 500 is in 1/kg^0.5), and the warning names that number; a result whose unit follows from the units written is not, such as the constant c of p*V^(-1) = c, or C in C = p_1*V_1^1.3 with a ratio r = 5 in V_1 = r*V_2. A unit with a fractional exponent is warned on only through a root, so p_1 = 100 in that line is not named either. The base of a power takes a unit only when its exponents are whole, so V in KE = 0.5*m*V^2 with KE = 500 is left without one. An exponent within 1e-9 of a multiple of 1e-6 is that multiple, so W = C*(V_2^(-0.3) - V_1^(-0.3))/(-0.3) with C = p_2*V_2^1.3 is an energy, though floating point leaves its exponent of m at 2.0000000000000004. An exponent made only of numbers is worked out, so V_2^(1 - 1.3) is V_2^(-0.3) and D = V^(1/3) with V in [m^3] is in m. A quantity shown in a unit of its own, such as K/s for a rate of temperature change, m³/s, m/s², N/m and W/(m·K) (in English units in an English sheet), is a usual one, except a thermal resistance (K/W) and a mass flux (kg/(m²·s)), which are shown in theirs but still warned on, since a heat rate or an area given without its unit makes one.
  • Unit conversion. Dividing by a unit gives a plain number in that unit: p_kPa = p / (1 [kPa]).
  • Other units. [ton] is the ton of refrigeration, 200 Btu/min, and [mile] is 5280 ft. [rpm] is revolutions per minute as a frequency, so omega = 2*pi*N with N in [rpm] is in rad/s, shown as 1/s. Electric current is a dimension of its own, with the units A, mA, V, kV and Ω (or ohm): a volt is a watt per ampere, so E*i is a power and E/i a resistance.
  • pi. pi is the constant π, unless the sheet has a line pi = …, which gives its own value.
  • Molar units. Amount of substance has the units mol, kmol and lbmol, so M = 28.01 [kg/kmol], n = m / M and R_u = 8.314 [kJ/kmol/K] carry checked units. Molar quantities are shown in kmol, or lbmol in English units.
  • Values shown. SI or English in the header sets the units results are shown in.

Temperatures and temperature changes

[C], [K], [F] or [R] alone is a temperature. Dome holds temperatures in kelvin, so a ratio such as T_2 / T_1 is a ratio of absolute temperatures. A change in temperature is written in [K] or [R]: T_1 + 20 [K] with T_1 = 27 [C] is 47 °C. A [C] or [F] number in a sum or difference is written in parentheses, (25 [C]) + dT, and a bare one there is refused, because a change typed in °C is the usual slip. Dome works in kelvin, so a conversion by hand, T_H + 273.15 [K], is refused: it would count the offset twice. A negative value in [K] or [R], such as dT = -10 [K], is a change.

A name makes no difference: dT = 10 [C] is the temperature 10 °C, and a change of 10 K is dT = 10 [K]. A value given in [K] or [R] is an amount in kelvin, shown in the unit typed, and is a temperature or a change as the equations use it. A sum of temperatures is a temperature only as an average, such as (T_1 + T_2)/2, and a change when its coefficients add to 0, as in T_2 - T_1; T_1 + T_2 used as it stands is refused. A value is shown in °C only where the equations make it a temperature for certain, such as the T of a state or of a property function; T_1 from p*v_1 = R*T_1 may be a temperature or a change, and is shown in K, which reads correctly either way. A change given as the T of a state or of a property function, such as T_x after T_x = T_a - T_b, is an error on its line: read as a temperature, a change of 30 K would be a temperature of 30 K.

Comments and sections

Text after % is a comment. %% at the start of a line begins a section in published reports; the first section's text is the report's default title.

%% Boundary work
% Equations can be written in any order.
W = p * (V_2 - V_1)    % work done by the gas

Checks and starting values

  • check compares two expressions after the sheet is solved: check V_2 > V_1. The comparisons are ==, <=, >=, < and >. The result appears at the right of the line and under the Checks tab. The two sides are checked for units as an equation's are, so check T_1 > 5 [bar] is an error on its line and check T_1 > 300 needs a unit after the 300; a check line with an error is not evaluated.
  • Two answers. When two values of a variable satisfy an equation, as for x^2 - 5*x + 6 = 0, a check line on that variable chooses between them: with check x > 2.5, Dome uses 3. Without one, Dome uses the value its iteration reaches from the starting value and names both values in a warning on the line, with a check line that chooses between them; a value of the other sign, such as the negative speed from V_2^2, is not counted. Dome reports a second value when its search of one equation finds one: equations solved together are not searched, and the search can miss a value close to the one used, so a line with no warning may still have a second answer.
  • guess sets the starting value of a variable found by iteration: guess T_2 = 400 [K]. Dome takes a starting value from the units of each unknown, never from its name: 5 % above the median of the known values in the same units, or else 300 K for a temperature, 1 bar for a pressure, 100 kJ/kg for a specific energy and so on, 0.5 for a value without units and 0.005 for a humidity ratio given to a moist-air function. A sheet rarely needs a guess line. One is for a solve that Dome reports could not start, or found no solution from its starting values. A guess line gives only the start: with two answers, the warning stays until a check line chooses.

Functions

A function is a formula written once and used in several places. It takes one line: the word function, a name, the parameters in parentheses, and one expression.

function cp_air(T) = 1.0 [kJ/kg/K] + 1e-4 [kJ/kg/K^2]*(T - 300 [K])
q = cp_air(T_2)*(T_2 - T_1)
  • Calls. A call gives one argument for each parameter, in order. Dome replaces each call with the body, the arguments in place of the parameters, before it solves the sheet, so a call may sit in any equation, state line or check, and an unknown may sit inside it. Units are worked out for each call, so function sq(a) = a*a gives m² from sq(2 [m]) and s² from sq(3 [s]).
  • The body. The body may use the parameters, numbers with units, math and property functions, other functions of the sheet and the sheet's variables. A sheet variable in the body is an input of every call.
  • Names. A function cannot call itself, directly or through another function. Its name cannot be a built-in function such as h or ln, a keyword such as state, or a variable of the sheet.
  • Problems. An error inside the body, such as a number without a unit, is reported on the line of the call and names the function. A call that, written out with every call inside it expanded, has more than 20000 symbols is refused: each nested call that uses its parameter twice doubles the length.

Tables

A table holds data given as rows of numbers, such as rows copied from a property table. The header line names the table and each column with its unit; the rows follow on indented lines, numbers separated by commas. A blank or unindented line ends the table, and a % comment may follow a row or stand on an indented line of its own. Problem 3.41 of Moran and Shapiro, with the rows of Table A-10 around the final state:

table a10 : T [C], v_g [m^3/kg], u_g [kJ/kg]
  12, 0.0460, 233.63
  16, 0.0405, 235.78
interp(a10, v_g, T = T_2) = v_1
u_2 = interp(a10, u_g, T = T_2)
  • interp. interp(a10, u_g, T = T_2) is the value of column u_g at T = T_2, by linear interpolation between the two rows around it, as by hand from a printed table. The key column, here T, must increase or decrease throughout. A key outside the table is an error that gives the table's range.
  • Unknowns. An unknown may sit in the key, so a table is read in either direction: the first line above finds T_2 from v_g = v_1. When the column read rises and falls, two keys give the same value, and Dome reports both, as for any equation with two answers.
  • Units. Each column carries its unit into the units check. A column in [C] or [F] is a temperature, and a key that the equations make a change for certain, such as T_2 - T_1 after T_1 = 20 [C] and T_2 = 70 [C], is an error on its line. A column in [K] or [R] is an amount in kelvin, whatever its name, and is read by value.

Problems

A line Dome cannot use is underlined in the sheet, and the Problems tab lists it with its line number and the reason. Holding the pointer over the underline shows the reason in the sheet. Below, the line Q = W + dU was added to the first example; nothing else in the sheet determines dU, so the sheet has fewer equations than unknowns.

The Math view

The Math view shows the sheet typeset as equations, with the value of each line. It is available in two places: the Code and Math buttons in the sheet's header switch the sheet pane, and the pane menu of any other pane can show Math beside the sheet, as above.

Keys and completion

With the cursor in the sheet, ⌘Enter (CtrlEnter on Windows and Linux) solves it; in the sweep editor the same keys run the sweep. With Auto-solve checked in the header, the sheet is solved after each edit. CtrlSpace completes a name, unit or fluid; on macOS, where CtrlSpace often switches the input source, Option` does the same.

Language reference

Help › Reference opens this reference in a pane beside the current panes. The text below is taken from that pane when this manual is built, so the two always match. Keys are listed as on macOS; on Windows and Linux, Ctrl takes the place of ⌘.

Statements

a = b + cEquation. Unknowns may appear on either side; the sheet is solved as a system.
x = 3; y = 4One statement per line, or separated by semicolons.
% textComment. %% at the start of a line begins a section in published reports.
fluid waterFluid for the states that follow: water, r134a, r22, ammonia, propane, air, and the ideal gases of Table A-23: nitrogen (n2), oxygen (o2), carbondioxide (co2), carbonmonoxide (co), water_ig (h2o_ig, water vapor on the basis of A-23, not the steam tables).
state 1 : p = …, T = …State from two independent properties among p, T, v, u, h, s, x. Defines p_1, T_1, v_1, u_1, h_1, s_1, x_1.
state 2 (r134a) : …State of a fluid other than the current one.
check a == bComparison evaluated after solving; also <=, >=, <, >. Its two sides are checked for units as an equation's are. A check on a variable chooses between two values that satisfy its equation.
guess T_2 = 400 [K]Starting value for a variable found by iteration, in place of the one Dome takes from its units (never from its name). Needed only when Dome reports that a solve could not start or found no solution from its starting values. It does not choose between two values; a check line does.
plot Ts : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3Property diagram: Ts, Tv, pv, ph or hs. Tv and pv have v on a logarithmic axis.
function f(x) = 2*x + 1Function on one line, called as f(a_2) in any equation, state line or check. The body may use the parameters, other functions and the sheet's variables. A function cannot call itself.
table cp_data : T [K], cp [kJ/kg/K]Table of data: a header line with each column's name and unit, then indented rows of numbers separated by commas. A blank or unindented line ends it. A column in C or F is a temperature; one in K or R is an amount in kelvin, whatever its name.

Units

80 [bar]A unit follows a number in brackets. Values are converted to SI internally.
480 [C]A temperature unit alone (C, K, F, R) is a temperature. A change in temperature is written in K or R: T_1 + 10 [K]. In a sum or difference, a C or F number is written in parentheses: (25 [C]) + dT. Dome works in kelvin, so 273.15 is never added by hand. A name makes no difference: dT = 10 [C] is the temperature 10 °C. A value given in K or R is an amount in kelvin, shown in the unit typed, a temperature or a change as the equations use it.
T_2 - T_1A difference of two temperatures is a change, shown in K (°R in English units). A temperature plus or minus a change is a temperature. An average such as (T_1 + T_2)/2 is a temperature; T_1 + T_2 used as it stands is refused. A value the equations do not make a temperature for certain, such as T_1 in p*v_1 = R*T_1, is shown in K. A change given as the T of a state or property function is an error.
T_1 - 20 [C]Refused: a bare C or F number in a sum or difference could be a temperature or a change. Write T_1 - 20 [K] for 20 K below T_1, and T_1 - (20 [C]) for the change from 20 °C. Set equal to a change it is refused too, as in T_2 - T_1 = 30 [C]: a change of 30 °C is 30 [K].
[kJ/kg·K]Everything after a slash is in the denominator. Also *, ^ and parentheses.
[kg/kmol]Amount of substance is a dimension of its own: mol, kmol, lbmol. Molar quantities are shown in kmol (lbmol in English units): h_bar = 8669 [kJ/kmol], R_u = 8.314 [kJ/kmol/K].
[V] [A] [Ω]Electric current is a dimension of its own: V, kV, A, mA, Ω (or ohm). A volt is a watt per ampere, so E*i is a power.
[rpm]Revolutions per minute, a frequency: omega = 2*pi*N is in rad/s, shown as 1/s. [ton] is the ton of refrigeration (200 Btu/min), [mile] 5280 ft.
piThe constant π, unless the sheet has a line pi = ….
unitskg g lb m cm mm ft in mile s min h rpm K C F R N kN lbf Pa kPa MPa bar atm psi J kJ MJ Btu kWh W kW MW hp ton L gal mol kmol lbmol A mA V kV Ω ohm

Functions

h(water, p = p_2, s = s_1)Property of a fluid at a state given by two named properties. Also p, T, v, u, s, x, cp, cv, rho. Each input has the units of its property and is checked as on a state line: T = 300 needs a unit.
Tsat(water, p = 1 [bar])Saturation temperature; psat(water, T = …) is the saturation pressure.
M(nitrogen)Molar mass of a fluid, in kg/kmol.
omega(moistair, p = 1 [atm], T = 25 [C], phi = 0.5)Moist air, from p and a pair from T, phi, omega, Twb, Tdp, pv, h; for a pair that does not work, Dome names the pairs that do. Functions: omega (humidity ratio), phi (relative humidity, a fraction), T, Twb (wet bulb), Tdp (dew point), pv (vapor partial pressure), and h, v, s, cp per kg of dry air. Moist air has no state lines. In English units moist air's h counts the dry air from 0 °F (Fig. A-9E), in SI from 0 °C (Fig. A-9). Each table's h, u and s count from its own reference, carried through the equations like units: water on the steam tables; air (h(air, …), a state of air), the gases of Table A-23 and a heat capacity times an absolute temperature (cp_a*T_1) from 0 K; moist air from its dry air at 0 °C and water on the steam tables; a difference of temperatures from none; an unknown h, or one typed from a table, takes only the reference its equation still requires, so in m_a*h_a1 + m_w*h_w1 = m_a*h_a2 + m_w*h_w2 h_w2 is on the steam tables. An equation that takes water from both the steam tables and water_ig, or dry air from both h(air, …) and moist air, is an error. An equation or a difference whose sides are on different references is an error, so every stream is written one way: every stream with h(moistair, …), or every stream with cp_a*(T - T_0) + omega*h(water, T = …, x = 1); and Moran's vapor is h(water, T = …, x = 1) (h_v = h_g(T)), not h(water_ig, …).
interp(cp_data, cp, T = T_1)Column cp of a table at T = T_1, by linear interpolation between rows. The key column must increase or decrease throughout, and a key outside the table is an error. A column in C or F holds temperatures, so a key that is a change for certain is an error; a column in K or R is read by value. An unknown may sit in the key.
ln exp sqrt absAlso log10, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, min, max.

Plot paths

-p- -s- -T- -v- -h-Process at constant pressure, entropy, temperature, specific volume or enthalpy. Drawn dashed when that property differs between the two states.
--Straight line.

Sweep

sweep T_3 = 320:20:600 [C]     % start:step:stop, or a list: 5, 7, 9
record eta, x_4
plot eta, x_4 vs T_3

The swept variable must be an input: a line name = number [unit], or a number written in a state line (x = 0 in state 3 makes x_3 an input).

sweep r = 2:1:12               % two sweep lines: every combination
sweep k = 1.3, 1.35, 1.4
plot eta vs r                  % one curve for each k

With two sweep lines each plot is drawn against one of the swept variables, with one curve for each value of the other; there are at most 2000 runs.

Properties

CoolProp 7.2.1dev (Helmholtz equations of state; air and the gases of Table A-23 as ideal gases with variable specific heats; moist air from its humid-air model, with h of dry air zero at 0 °C on SI sheets, as on the psychrometric chart (Fig. A-9), and at 0 °F on English sheets (Fig. A-9E)). Enthalpy, internal energy and entropy are shifted to the reference states of the Moran and Shapiro tables. Differences between states, and the cycle results built from them, agree closely with the tables; a single value can differ from the printed table by about 1 kJ/kg, and by up to about 5 kJ/kg in parts of the superheated tables. Answers graded in ENES232 use the printed tables.

Keys

⌘EnterSolve, with the cursor in the sheet; in the sweep editor, run the sweep
⌘S, ⌘⇧SSave, save as
⌘O, ⌘NOpen, new
⌘Z, ⌘⇧ZUndo, redo
Ctrl+Space, ⌥`Complete a name, unit or fluid, in the sheet or the sweep editor
